quotes.text: if your data is a chaotic wreck of un-mapped files, no amount of clever phrasing will save the output. You are essentially asking a genius to search through a dumpster.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures in one image why prompt tricks cannot fix a disorganized data estate.

quotes.text: Stale data is actually worse than no data. If the AI finds nothing, you go look for it yourself. But if the AI finds the wrong thing and presents it confidently, you make a bad decision.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: In the old world, security was about who could open a specific folder. In the AI world, security is about what the model is allowed to learn from.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: You cannot scale 1,000 different people writing 1,000 different prompts. You can, however, scale 10 well-designed lattices that handle 10 core business processes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the case for shared architecture over individual prompt skills.

quotes.text: When you realize that co-pilot is just the interface for this entire stack, your strategy changes. You stop training people on how to type and start training your architects on how to build.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shifts the Copilot rollout focus from end-user prompt training to architecture.

chapters.title: The structural rot: why context collapses
Replacing the prompt with the decision lattice
The architecture beyond the interface: Graph, Purview, Entra ID, Fabric, Copilot Studio

takeaways: Copilot results fail in production mostly because of fragmented context, mis-scoped permissions and stale duplicate files, not because of weak prompts.
A reliable AI coworker is built from layers of signals, curated context via Graph connectors, governed decision logic in Copilot Studio and guardrails from Purview and Entra ID.
Success should be measured by time to decision, rework rate and exception count, and the model can be proven on one workflow in 30 days.
hook: Many organizations train employees to write better prompts while Copilot keeps pulling stale, overshared or fragmented data. This episode shows IT leaders and Microsoft 365 architects how to replace prompt hacks with a governed architecture built on Microsoft Graph, Purview, Entra ID, Fabric and Copilot Studio, and how to prove its value with decision-focused metrics in 30 days.
